PROP
44
REQUIRES COMMUNITY HEALTH CLINICS SPEND 90% OF REVENUE ON PROGRAM SERVICES. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Imposes penalties on nonprofit Federally Qualified Health Centers (community clinics providing primary care to medically underserved areas and populations) that spend less than 90% of revenue on “program services” advancing their charitable purpose, including but not limited to patient services. Fiscal Impact: Increased state costs in the low tens of millions of dollars per year, covered by fees. Supporters: None submitted Opponents: American Academy of Pediatrics CA; CA School Nurses Org; CA Academy of Family Physicians; CA Medical Assoc.
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Certain private nonprofit health care clinics would have to spend at least 90 percent of their revenue each year on providing health care services.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: The new requirement on health care clinic spending would not go into effect.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Prop. 44 holds community clinics and their executives accountable by requiring that 90% of clinic revenue be spent on clinics’ charitable mission: patient care and services that make care possible. It increases transparency, reduces wasteful executive spending, and ensures healthcare dollars go where they belong: caring for Californians in need.
CON
Prop. 44 is a dangerous measure that will shut down hundreds of community health clinics and eliminate vital patient services for millions of Californians. American Academy of Pediatrics CA, California Medical Association, California Academy of Family Physicians, California School Nurses Organization, doctors, nurses and patients urge NO on 44! www.NOProp44.com

# Proposition 44
Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% of Revenue on Program Services.
Initiative Statute.
## Analysis of Measure
### Proposal
***Sets Minimum Spending on Health Care at Private Nonprofit Safety Net Clinics.*** Proposition 44 requires private nonprofit safety net clinics to spend at least 90 percent of their total revenue each year on providing health care services.
This means that spending on other expenses, such as administrative costs, would be limited to no more than 10 percent of revenue.
The California Attorney General would define in more detail which kinds of expenses are related to providing health care services, and which are other expenses, using existing reports to the federal government as a starting point.
Affected clinics could ask the state for a temporary waiver of the requirements in some cases.
***Creates Penalty for Falling Short of Minimum.*** Proposition 44 requires affected clinics to pay a penalty to the state if they fall short of the new health care spending minimum.
The penalty would equal the amount of spending needed to reach the 90 percent minimum.
Clinics could get their money back if they comply with the spending requirements within five years.
If clinics do not comply within five years, the state would keep the money and spend it on clinic workforce programs.

# Proposition 44: Community Health Clinics
## Proposition 44: Requires Community Health Clinics to Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services. Initiative Statute.
...
### Summary
Proposition 44 began as Initiative 25-0008, filed by Shawna Brown and Sean Fleming in July 2025.
After receiving its official title and summary, the measure was cleared for signature gathering in October 2025.
On May 18, 2026, the Secretary of State determined through a random sample that the measure had enough valid signatures to become eligible for the ballot.
It was formally certified for the November 3, 2026, statewide ballot on June 25, 2026, and subsequently designated Proposition 44.
Proposition 44 would require certain private nonprofit safety net clinics in California to spend at least 90% of their total revenue each year on providing health care services.
No more than 10% could be spent on administrative and other expenses that do not qualify as health care services.
The California Attorney General would establish more comprehensive rules for determining which expenses count toward the 90% requirement, and affected clinics could seek temporary waivers in certain circumstances.
Clinics that fail to meet the 90% spending requirement would have to pay a penalty to the state for an amount equal to the shortfall.
The clinic could be reimbursed if it comes into compliance within five years.
If it does not meet the requirements, the state would keep the money and use it to support workforce programs

# PROP 44: The Clinic Funding Accountability and Transparency Act
###### Quick Facts
- **Official ballot title:** “Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% of Revenue on Program Services.
Initiative Statute” (circulating title and summary issued by the attorney general, October 7, 2025).
The measure’s own name is the “Clinic Funding Accountability and Transparency Act.”
- **Type:** Initiated state statute (AG No. 25-0008A1).
It adds new sections to the Government Code and the Health and Safety Code.
It is not a constitutional amendment.
- **A vote YES means:** Nonprofit federally qualified health centers must spend at least 90 percent of their total annual revenue on mission-related “program services” or pay a penalty equal to the shortfall.
Clinics must report the underlying figures to the attorney general, who publishes a “mission spend ratio” for each clinic.
- **A vote NO means:** No revenue-spending floor is imposed on these clinics.
Their spending stays governed by existing nonprofit and federal-grant rules and by their own boards.
- **Sponsor/proponent:** Californians for Responsible Healthcare, sponsored by SEIU-UHW West (Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West).
Proponents of record are Shawna Brown and Sean Fleming.

PROP
44
REQUIRES COMMUNITY HEALTH CLINICS SPEND 90% OF REVENUE ON PROGRAM SERVICES. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Imposes penalties on nonprofit Federally Qualified Health Centers (community clinics providing primary care to medically underserved areas and populations) that spend less than 90% of revenue on “program services” advancing their charitable purpose, including but not limited to patient services. Fiscal Impact: Increased state costs in the low tens of millions of dollars per year, covered by fees. Supporters: None submitted Opponents: American Academy of Pediatrics CA; CA School Nurses Org; CA Academy of Family Physicians; CA Medical Assoc.
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Certain private nonprofit health care clinics would have to spend at least 90 percent of their revenue each year on providing health care services.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: The new requirement on health care clinic spending would not go into effect.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Prop. 44 holds community clinics and their executives accountable by requiring that 90% of clinic revenue be spent on clinics’ charitable mission: patient care and services that make care possible. It increases transparency, reduces wasteful executive spending, and ensures healthcare dollars go where they belong: caring for Californians in need.
CON
Prop. 44 is a dangerous measure that will shut down hundreds of community health clinics and eliminate vital patient services for millions of Californians. American Academy of Pediatrics CA, California Medical Association, California Academy of Family Physicians, California School Nurses Organization, doctors, nurses and patients urge NO on 44! www.NOProp44.com

# Proposition 44
Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% of Revenue on Program Services.
Initiative Statute.
## Analysis of Measure
### Proposal
***Sets Minimum Spending on Health Care at Private Nonprofit Safety Net Clinics.*** Proposition 44 requires private nonprofit safety net clinics to spend at least 90 percent of their total revenue each year on providing health care services.
This means that spending on other expenses, such as administrative costs, would be limited to no more than 10 percent of revenue.
The California Attorney General would define in more detail which kinds of expenses are related to providing health care services, and which are other expenses, using existing reports to the federal government as a starting point.
Affected clinics could ask the state for a temporary waiver of the requirements in some cases.
***Creates Penalty for Falling Short of Minimum.*** Proposition 44 requires affected clinics to pay a penalty to the state if they fall short of the new health care spending minimum.
The penalty would equal the amount of spending needed to reach the 90 percent minimum.
Clinics could get their money back if they comply with the spending requirements within five years.
If clinics do not comply within five years, the state would keep the money and spend it on clinic workforce programs.

### Summary
Proposition 44 began as Initiative 25-0008, filed by Shawna Brown and Sean Fleming in July 2025.
After receiving its official title and summary, the measure was cleared for signature gathering in October 2025.
On May 18, 2026, the Secretary of State determined through a random sample that the measure had enough valid signatures to become eligible for the ballot.
It was formally certified for the November 3, 2026, statewide ballot on June 25, 2026, and subsequently designated Proposition 44.
Proposition 44 would require certain private nonprofit safety net clinics in California to spend at least 90% of their total revenue each year on providing health care services.
No more than 10% could be spent on administrative and other expenses that do not qualify as health care services.
The California Attorney General would establish more comprehensive rules for determining which expenses count toward the 90% requirement, and affected clinics could seek temporary waivers in certain circumstances.
Clinics that fail to meet the 90% spending requirement would have to pay a penalty to the state for an amount equal to the shortfall.
The clinic could be reimbursed if it comes into compliance within five years.
If it does not meet the requirements, the state would keep the money and use it to support workforce programs

Oct. 1, 2026
...
If the proposition passes, the state attorney general will be responsible for determining what services fall into that category.
If spending on administrative or non-healthcare functions exceeded 10% of total revenue, a clinic would have to pay a penalty equal to the amount it overspent.

PROP
44
REQUIRES COMMUNITY HEALTH CLINICS SPEND 90% OF REVENUE ON PROGRAM SERVICES. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Imposes penalties on nonprofit Federally Qualified Health Centers (community clinics providing primary care to medically underserved areas and populations) that spend less than 90% of revenue on “program services” advancing their charitable purpose, including but not limited to patient services. Fiscal Impact: Increased state costs in the low tens of millions of dollars per year, covered by fees. Supporters: None submitted Opponents: American Academy of Pediatrics CA; CA School Nurses Org; CA Academy of Family Physicians; CA Medical Assoc.
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Certain private nonprofit health care clinics would have to spend at least 90 percent of their revenue each year on providing health care services.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: The new requirement on health care clinic spending would not go into effect.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Prop. 44 holds community clinics and their executives accountable by requiring that 90% of clinic revenue be spent on clinics’ charitable mission: patient care and services that make care possible. It increases transparency, reduces wasteful executive spending, and ensures healthcare dollars go where they belong: caring for Californians in need.
CON
Prop. 44 is a dangerous measure that will shut down hundreds of community health clinics and eliminate vital patient services for millions of Californians. American Academy of Pediatrics CA, California Medical Association, California Academy of Family Physicians, California School Nurses Organization, doctors, nurses and patients urge NO on 44! www.NOProp44.com

### Proposal
***Sets Minimum Spending on Health Care at Private Nonprofit Safety Net Clinics.*** Proposition 44 requires private nonprofit safety net clinics to spend at least 90 percent of their total revenue each year on providing health care services.
This means that spending on other expenses, such as administrative costs, would be limited to no more than 10 percent of revenue.
The California Attorney General would define in more detail which kinds of expenses are related to providing health care services, and which are other expenses, using existing reports to the federal government as a starting point.
Affected clinics could ask the state for a temporary waiver of the requirements in some cases.
***Creates Penalty for Falling Short of Minimum.*** Proposition 44 requires affected clinics to pay a penalty to the state if they fall short of the new health care spending minimum.
The penalty would equal the amount of spending needed to reach the 90 percent minimum.
Clinics could get their money back if they comply with the spending requirements within five years.
If clinics do not comply within five years, the state would keep the money and spend it on clinic workforce programs.

California's community health clinics are facing a 90% spending rule under Proposition 44, which would penalize nonprofit clinics that spend less on patient services.
